topic: Proof of Snell's Law: The Principle of Least Time

outline.topic: Proof of Snell's Law: The Principle of Least Time

sections.title: Introduction: The Lifeguard Dilemma (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Use a visual analogy: A lifeguard on the beach needs to reach a drowning swimmer in the water. Running on sand is faster than swimming. Should they run in a straight line, or aim for a point that minimizes total time?
sections.example: An animation showing a lifeguard choosing between a straight path (shorter distance, slower speed) vs. a refracted path (longer distance, higher speed).

sections.title: Prerequisite: Fermat’s Principle (0:45-1:30)
sections.content: Introduce Fermat's Principle of Least Time: Light travels between two points along the path that takes the least amount of time. Define v1 = c/n1 and v2 = c/n2 (velocity in two media).
sections.example: A graphic showing the wavefronts changing speed at the interface, demonstrating that 'shortest path' in time $\neq$ 'shortest path' in distance.

sections.title: Mathematical Modeling (1:30-3:00)
sections.content: Set up a coordinate system at the interface. Define point A (0, h1) and point B (x, -h2). Let the refracted point be (y, 0). Express Total Time T(y) = sqrt(h1^2 + y^2)/v1 + sqrt(h2^2 + (x-y)^2)/v2.
sections.example: An interactive diagram where moving point (y, 0) dynamically updates the calculated Time T graph, highlighting the global minimum.

sections.title: Derivation: The Calculus of Refraction (3:00-4:15)
sections.content: Take the derivative dT/dy and set it to zero. Using the geometric definition of sine (sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse), show that dT/dy = sin(θ1)/v1 - sin(θ2)/v2 = 0.
sections.example: Side-by-side split screen: Left shows the geometric triangle at the interface; Right shows the algebraic steps resulting in (sin θ1)/v1 = (sin θ2)/v2.

sections.title: Synthesis & Snell's Law (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Substitute v = c/n into the result to reach n1 sin(θ1) = n2 sin(θ2). Summarize that light's 'intelligence' is actually just nature optimizing for time.
sections.example: A final visual of a laser beam passing through a glass block, with labels showing how the refractive indices directly dictate the bending angles proven by the math.

storyboard.title: Introduction: The Lifeguard Dilemma (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Lifeguard must reach swimmer in water.
Running on sand is faster than swimming.
Straight path is longer in water.
Refracted path minimizes total travel time.
Nature chooses the fastest route.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Fermat’s Principle (0:45-1:30)
lecture_lines: Light follows the path of least time.
Fermat's Principle defines this path.
Speed depends on the refractive index.

storyboard.title: Mathematical Modeling (1:30-3:00)
lecture_lines: Place interface at the origin.
Define points A and B.
Express total time as a function.
Find the path minimizing total time.
This reveals the path geometry.

storyboard.title: Derivation: The Calculus of Refraction (3:00-4:15)
lecture_lines: Differentiate total time with respect to position.
Set derivative to zero for minimum.
This yields the geometric sine relationship.
Sine ratio equals velocity ratio.
Geometric proof of refraction law.

storyboard.title: Synthesis & Snell's Law (4:15-5:00)
lecture_lines: Use velocity definitions with indices.
Derive Snell's Law equation.
Nature optimizes for time efficiency.
